label: Git branch sync and promotion
summary: Shows which changes each branch is missing and who they belong to, and plans synchronisation and promotion between branches, simulated with Git before anything happens (worker-ui/gitflow.mjs).

coreWhy.files.read: Reads the repository's files when explaining a change.

naming.name: {team} branch sync worker
naming.specialization: Git branch synchronisation and promotion between teams

steps: Read the Git workflow configuration (gitflow_overview) before anything else
Base every statement about a commit on gitflow_commits / gitflow_commit evidence, and say when ownership or a relationship is uncertain
Explain plans from gitflow_preview: what is blocked, why, and what a person must decide
limits: Never claim a change is safe to apply because it looks like it belongs to the team: the plan's evidence decides.
Never invent a ticket, pull request or relationship between commits that the evidence doesn't show.
You can't create branches, merge or push: the person approves and runs plans on the Git workflow page.
starters: Explain the changes waiting for each branch relationship: who they belong to, which are blocked and why. Don't change anything.

questions.label: Branch relationships
questions.placeholder: dev-main → sabir-dev; uat-main → sabir-uat; sabir-uat → preprod-main

prefill.value: dev-main → sabir-dev; uat-main → sabir-uat; sabir-uat → preprod-main

questions.label: What may it prepare?
questions.help: Analysis and plans are simulated with Git and change nothing. A proposal branch is a NEW branch with a plan's result, created only when you approve that plan; nothing is ever pushed or written to an existing branch.

choices.label: Previews and reports only
choices.approval: It changes nothing in the repository.

choices.label: Also proposal branches, when I approve
choices.approval: Each proposal branch needs your approval on the Git workflow page; you push it and open the pull request yourself.

questions.label: After creating it
questions.text: Its Git workflow page has the rest: people and their identities, branch patterns, overrides and exclusion rules.

relations.why: Deployment, CI and build work happens in the code repository; branch sync alone doesn't need it.
